source.title: NLEBench+NorGLM: A Comprehensive Empirical Analysis and Benchmark Dataset for Generative Language Models in Norwegian
source.authors: Peng Liu; Le-Mei Zhang; T. Farup; Even W. Lauvrak; Jon Espen Ingvaldsen; Simen Eide; J. A. Gulla; Zhirong Yang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some table formatting is flattened, so ambiguous values have not been assigned to rows.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream task performance across differently sized models, providing a conceptual test of V6. It does not measure pretraining loss scaling or compute-optimal allocations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream scores for models of different sizes and discusses whether the larger models have an advantage. It does not report held-out pretraining cross-entropy across parameter, token, or compute sweeps, extrapolation from smaller runs, or compute-optimal allocations. Its mention of Hoffmann et al. is cited prior work, not a result row. Ambiguous results in Table 3 are omitted because the flattened table does not securely map all values to model names.
record.test_reason: The study trains NorGPT-369M, 3B and 23B on the same 196G Norwegian-centred corpus and compares their downstream scores. This is a parameter-size series in a new, data-constrained, low-resource setting, and it bears on V6 (downstream gains with scale). It has only three points, no fit, and no loss-based prediction. The other models differ in architecture or training history, so they are not part of the size series.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors conclude that larger parameter scale had limited impact on downstream performance when the pretraining data is small; the 23B model lacked the expected absolute advantage. They say this supports Hoffmann et al., but data size was never varied, so the data explanation is untested. They also note NB-GPT-J-6B is consistent and has the best perplexity, and that smaller models show useful abilities, including chain-of-thought.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and evaluates Norwegian models at different scales and reports downstream benchmark scores; it does not use the original studies' held-out pretraining loss scaling fits or fixed-compute allocation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by downstream dataset, metric, architecture, and training history; the authors also note that limited pretraining data constrains performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Chain-of-thought gains on NO-Multi-QA-Sum showed no clear correlation with model size (Tables 4-5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gains from chain-of-thought prompting grow with model scale.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The evidence relevant to V6 consists of downstream benchmark scores rather than held-out pretraining loss or fitted predictive laws. Comparisons include different architectures and training histories, and no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 results were omitted because the flattened header/value layout does not securely assign all reported values to model names. Other metrics from Tables 2, 13, and 14 were omitted to stay within the row limit and focus on BLEU, PPL, and accuracy; the paper reports additional metrics including ROUGE, Dist-4, MAUVE, and F1.

untested.parts: Prediction of downstream scores from pretraining loss; any fitted scale-to-performance law. Only three sizes are compared, all on one fixed dataset.
No compute-allocation sweep; Hoffmann et al. is only cited.
No fixed-size shape comparison of loss.

missing.what: NO-CNN/DailyMail summarization scores for the NorGPT size series. Inferred column order gives BLEU 2.38/2.61/1.90 and ROUGE-1 20.97/20.31/22.44 (369M/3B/23B); the mapping should be verified.
Other ConvAI2 metrics: ROUGE-1 16.94/17.09/16.72 and MAUVE 0.56/0.87/0.64; 23B falls below 3B.
NLU F1 scores, where NorGPT-23B is best in the series (e.g. MRPC F1 54.5/46.1/64.4).
NO-Multi-QA-Sum results comparing NorGPT-3B and 23B. Authors say performance there appears proportional to size.

record.verdict_notes: Only the NorGPT-369M/3B/23B rows form a valid size series: same data, same architecture family. The NorLlama, continued-training, NB-GPT-J-6B and GPT-3.5 rows were relinked to none. No uncertainty estimates or repeated runs are reported, so small differences such as QNLI 75.8 vs 76.4 may be noise.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or predictions of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or fitted allocation trends.
No controlled comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count for pretraining loss.
No tests of scaling-law form in other modalities or training regimes.
Tests downstream benchmark scores across model sizes, but does not test prediction from pretraining loss or fit a scale-to-performance law.
Does not compare fitted scaling exponents or fitting choices, nor test bending away from a fitted power law.

relationships.condition: NorGPT series (369M, 3B, 23B, same 196G data) on NLU accuracy (NO-BoolQ, NO-QNLI) and NO-Alpaca perplexity
relationships.reason: Scores rise with size: BoolQ 58.6/60.6/63.2, QNLI 75.8/76.4/79.7, PPL 9.83/6.62/6.15 (r21, r24, r27, r30, r15, r18). Gains are modest.
relationships.display_finding: BoolQ accuracy increased through 58.6, 60.6, and 63.2, QNLI through 75.8, 76.4, and 79.7, while perplexity decreased through 9.83, 6.62, and 6.15.

relationships.condition: Generation tasks and NO-MRPC, with pretraining data fixed at 196G
relationships.reason: Gains are non-monotonic: 3B falls below 369M on MRPC (r33), and 23B leads only on ConvAI2 BLEU, barely (r2, r5). Authors report the 23B model showed no expected absolute advantage.
relationships.display_finding: The 3B model underperformed 369M on MRPC, while 23B led only narrowly on ConvAI2 BLEU and lacked the expected overall advantage.

relationships.reason: Larger NorGPT models score lower BLEU than 369M: 2.91 vs 2.16 (3B) and 2.33 (23B) (r9, r12).
relationships.display_finding: BLEU was 2.91 at 369M, compared with 2.16 at 3B and 2.33 at 23B.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: NorGPT-family accuracy on NO-BoolQ and NO-QNLI, comparing NorGPT-369M, NorGPT-3B, and NorGPT-23B
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy increases across these three sizes on both tasks: NO-BoolQ 58.6, 60.6, 63.2 (r20, r21, r24) and NO-QNLI 75.8, 76.4, 79.7 (r26, r27, r30). This is limited evidence of improvement with size, not a fitted predictive law.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across the reported downstream tasks and model/training conditions
reader_labels.reason: The size-performance pattern is not uniform: the larger NorGPT-3B has lower NO-MRPC accuracy than NorGPT-369M (r32, r33), instruction-task BLEU is lower for NorGPT-3B than NorGPT-369M (r8, r9), and the paper reports that the 23B model did not show an expected absolute advantage across downstream tasks (r1-r19, r20-r37).
